# Dosage table

EPA+DHA doses by purpose. These are evidence-derived targets, not
prescriptions; the `0` row records that no supplement dose is justified by
current trial evidence.

| Purpose | EPA+DHA per day | Basis | What it does and does not do |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Population adequacy (no specific indication) | 250 mg | EFSA adequate intake | Equivalent to roughly two 4-oz servings of fatty fish per week; the basis for the EU heart claim. |
| Primary prevention in healthy adults | 0-1,000 mg | VITAL, ASCEND, Cochrane | No proven reduction in the primary composite. If a person takes 1 g/day, expect a possible MI reduction and no mortality benefit. |
| Secondary prevention after myocardial infarction | 1,000 mg | AHA and trial practice | Around 1 g/day is the dose used in most secondary-prevention trials; benefits are modest and mainly coronary. |
| Triglyceride lowering (moderate hypertriglyceridaemia) | 2,000-4,000 mg | AHA 2019 science advisory | 4 g/day gives 20-30%; 2 g/day gives roughly half that. Must be discussed with a clinician if TG >500 mg/dL. |
| Severe hypertriglyceridaemia (>=500 mg/dL) | 4,000 mg | AHA 2019; prescription products | Goal is TG <500 mg/dL to reduce pancreatitis risk. Prescription icosapent ethyl or omega-3-acid ethyl esters, not supplements. |
| Pregnancy (preterm birth risk reduction) | 500-1,000 mg | Cochrane 2018; expert summary | At least 500 mg DHA, started by about 12 weeks. ORIP (800 mg DHA) was null, so benefit is not universal. |
| Depression (adjunct only) | 1,000-2,000 mg | Meta-analysis and meta-regression | EPA-predominant formulations; never a substitute for evidence-based treatment. Low certainty. |
| Rheumatoid arthritis (adjunct) | 2,700-3,000 mg | Older positive trials | Trials showing NSAID-sparing used >=2.7 g/day; modern certainty-rated reviews find little clinical benefit. |
| Dry eye disease | 3,000 mg | DREAM trial | Tested and null at 3 g/day. Not recommended on current evidence. |
| Older adults seeking muscle preservation | 2,000-3,000 mg | Small RCTs | Effects are small and inconsistent; resistance training and protein intake matter far more. |
| General upper safety bound | 0-5,000 mg | FDA 2019; EFSA 2012 | No UL exists. Up to 5 g/day has FDA enforcement discretion for safety; above 5 g/day the evidence is insufficient. |
